q: Like air and water, ____ plays an essential role in our ecosystems.
e: Like air and water, soil plays an essential role in our ecosystems. Soil is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Earth's body of soil, called the ____, has four important functions including being a medium for plant growth and a habitat for organisms.
e: Earth's body of soil, called the pedosphere, has four important functions including being a medium for plant growth and a habitat for organisms. Pedosphere is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Soil is the upper layer of the Earth in which plants grow, typically consisting of a mixture of organic remains, clay and ____.
e: Soil is the upper layer of the Earth in which plants grow, typically consisting of a mixture of organic remains, clay and rock particles. Rock particles is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The three main layers of the soil with increasing depth are top soil, subsoil and ____.
e: The three main layers of the soil with increasing depth are top soil, subsoil and bedrock. Bedrock is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The sequence of the soil layers with increasing depth is called the ____.
e: The sequence of the soil layers with increasing depth is called the soil profile. Soil profile is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The top layer of soil is known as the top soil or the ____ layer, which is rich in organic materials.
e: The top layer of soil is known as the top soil or the humus layer, which is rich in organic materials. Humus is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The top soil has a dark brown colour because it consists of decomposed material and ____.
e: The top soil has a dark brown colour because it consists of decomposed material and organic matter. Organic matter is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The humus makes the top soil soft and ____ to hold enough air and water.
e: The humus makes the top soil soft and porous to hold enough air and water. Porous is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In the top soil layer, the seeds ____ and roots of the plants grow.
e: In the top soil layer, the seeds germinate and roots of the plants grow. Germinate is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Many living organisms like ____, bacteria and fungi are found in the top soil layer.
e: Many living organisms like earthworms, bacteria and fungi are found in the top soil layer. Earthworms is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Just below the top soil lies another layer called ____.
e: Just below the top soil lies another layer called subsoil. Subsoil is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The subsoil is comparatively harder and more ____ than top soil.
e: The subsoil is comparatively harder and more compact than top soil. Compact is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The subsoil is lighter in colour than the top soil because there is less ____ in this layer.
e: The subsoil is lighter in colour than the top soil because there is less humus in this layer. Humus is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The subsoil is less organic but is rich in ____ brought down from the top soil.
e: The subsoil is less organic but is rich in minerals brought down from the top soil. Minerals is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The subsoil contains metal salts, especially ____ in a large proportion.
e: The subsoil contains metal salts, especially iron oxide in a large proportion. Iron oxide is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The next layer is bedrock or ____, which lies just below the subsoil.
e: The next layer is bedrock or parent rock, which lies just below the subsoil. Parent rock is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Bedrock contains no ____ and is made up of stones and rocks, so it is very hard.
e: Bedrock contains no organic matter and is made up of stones and rocks, so it is very hard. Organic matter is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The mineral component of soil originates from the parent rocks by ____ processes.
e: The mineral component of soil originates from the parent rocks by weathering processes. Weathering is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The basic components of soil are mineral matter (45%), organic matter (5%), air (20~30%) and ____.
e: The basic components of soil are mineral matter (45%), organic matter (5%), air (20~30%) and water. Water is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Air and water occupy the ____ in soils.
e: Air and water occupy the pore spaces in soils. Pore spaces is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Pore spaces are the ____ between the soil particles.
e: Pore spaces are the voids between the soil particles. Voids is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Fine-textured soils have more total ____ than coarse-textured soils.
e: Fine-textured soils have more total pore space than coarse-textured soils. Pore space is the idea that completes this fact.

q: As soils absorb water, the ____ decreases.
e: As soils absorb water, the air space decreases. Air space is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Except for gravel and rocks, the three fractions of soil are sand, silt and ____.
e: Except for gravel and rocks, the three fractions of soil are sand, silt and clay. Clay is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The organic matter of soils is made up of undecomposed and partially decomposed residues of plants and animals and the tissue of living and dead ____.
e: The organic matter of soils is made up of undecomposed and partially decomposed residues of plants and animals and the tissue of living and dead microorganisms. Microorganisms is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Soil texture is characterised by the relative proportion of sand, silt and ____ separates found in the soil.
e: Soil texture is characterised by the relative proportion of sand, silt and clay separates found in the soil. Clay is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A coarse sand will feel gritty but a wet clay will feel heavy and ____.
e: A coarse sand will feel gritty but a wet clay will feel heavy and sticky. Sticky is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Soil is made up of different-sized particles, and ____ particles tend to be the biggest.
e: Soil is made up of different-sized particles, and sand particles tend to be the biggest. Sand is the idea that completes this fact.

q: ____ particles are very small.
e: Clay particles are very small. Clay is the idea that completes this fact.

q: If the proportion of sand in the soil is increased, the resultant soil becomes ____ in texture.
e: If the proportion of sand in the soil is increased, the resultant soil becomes coarser in texture. Coarser is the idea that completes this fact.

q: If the proportion of clay in the soil is increased, the resultant soil becomes ____ in texture.
e: If the proportion of clay in the soil is increased, the resultant soil becomes finer in texture. Finer is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The soil textural triangle is a classification system used to determine soil classes based on their ____.
e: The soil textural triangle is a classification system used to determine soil classes based on their physical texture. Physical texture is the idea that completes this fact.

q: There are ____ classes of soil texture as shown in the soil textural triangle.
e: There are twelve classes of soil texture as shown in the soil textural triangle. Twelve is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The term ____ refers to a soil with a combination of sand, silt and clay sized particles.
e: The term loam refers to a soil with a combination of sand, silt and clay sized particles. Loam is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A soil with 30% clay, 50% sand and 20% silt is called a ____.
e: A soil with 30% clay, 50% sand and 20% silt is called a sandy clay loam. Sandy clay loam is the idea that completes this fact.

q: One of the most important functions of soil in supporting plant growth is to provide essential plant nutrients: macro-nutrients and ____.
e: One of the most important functions of soil in supporting plant growth is to provide essential plant nutrients: macro-nutrients and micro-nutrients. Micro-nutrients is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Macro-nutrients are those elements that occur in ____ levels in plant materials or in fluids in the plant.
e: Macro-nutrients are those elements that occur in substantial levels in plant materials or in fluids in the plant. Substantial is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Micro-nutrients are elements that are essential only at very low levels and generally are required for the functioning of ____.
e: Micro-nutrients are elements that are essential only at very low levels and generally are required for the functioning of enzymes. Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up reactions in cells.

q: Essential macro-nutrients include carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, calcium, magnesium and ____.
e: Essential macro-nutrients include carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, calcium, magnesium and sulphur. Sulphur is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Essential micro-nutrients include boron, chlorine, copper, iron, manganese, molybdenum, zinc, sodium and ____.
e: Essential micro-nutrients include boron, chlorine, copper, iron, manganese, molybdenum, zinc, sodium and vanadium. Vanadium is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium (____) are plant nutrients that are obtained from soil.
e: Nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium (NPK) are plant nutrients that are obtained from soil. NPK is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium are so important for crop productivity that they are commonly added to soil as ____.
e: Nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium are so important for crop productivity that they are commonly added to soil as fertilisers. Fertilisers is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Nitrogen has the most dramatic effect on the ____ growth, especially in grass and cereal plants.
e: Nitrogen has the most dramatic effect on the leaf growth, especially in grass and cereal plants. Leaf is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Nitrogen is used to make ____ in plants.
e: Nitrogen is used to make protein in plants. Protein is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Nitrogen bound to soil ____ is especially important in maintaining soil fertility.
e: Nitrogen bound to soil humus is especially important in maintaining soil fertility. Humus is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Phosphorus is essential in the ____ of every cell, so growth cannot continue in its complete absence.
e: Phosphorus is essential in the nucleus of every cell, so growth cannot continue in its complete absence. The nucleus is the control centre of a eukaryotic cell.

q: Phosphorus is particularly associated with the development of a strong root system and ____ development.
e: Phosphorus is particularly associated with the development of a strong root system and floral development. Floral is the idea that completes this fact.

q: ____ is required at high levels for growing plants.
e: Potassium is required at high levels for growing plants. Potassium is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Potassium activates some enzymes and plays a key role in the ____ balance in plants.
e: Potassium activates some enzymes and plays a key role in the water balance in plants. Water is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Soil pH is a fundamental property that affects a surprisingly large range of chemical, physical and ____ processes in soils.
e: Soil pH is a fundamental property that affects a surprisingly large range of chemical, physical and biological processes in soils. Biological is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Soil pH is a measure of the ____ and alkalinity in soils.
e: Soil pH is a measure of the acidity and alkalinity in soils. Acidity is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The optimal pH range for most plants is between ____ and 7.0.
e: The optimal pH range for most plants is between 5.5 and 7.0. 5.5 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Soil pH is important because of its effect on the ____ of essential elements, or nutrients, in soils.
e: Soil pH is important because of its effect on the availability of essential elements, or nutrients, in soils. Availability is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Many elements can be taken up by plants more easily if the soil pH is near neutral to marginally ____.
e: Many elements can be taken up by plants more easily if the soil pH is near neutral to marginally acidic. pH measures how acidic or alkaline a solution is, with 7 as neutral.

q: If the soil is more acidic than the required pH, it can be treated by adding ____.
e: If the soil is more acidic than the required pH, it can be treated by adding lime. Lime is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Lime is ____ and it will neutralise the acidity of the soil and make it more neutral.
e: Lime is alkaline and it will neutralise the acidity of the soil and make it more neutral. Alkaline is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Alkali or alkaline soils are clay soils with high pH (____).
e: Alkali or alkaline soils are clay soils with high pH (>8.5). >8.5 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: ____ helps in the treatment of alkaline soils.
e: Gypsum helps in the treatment of alkaline soils. Gypsum is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Soil is the receptor of large quantities of waste products: domestic, human, animal, industrial and ____ products.
e: Soil is the receptor of large quantities of waste products: domestic, human, animal, industrial and agricultural products. Agricultural is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Combustion of sulphur-containing fuels in the smelting process emits ____, and finally leaves sulphate on the soil.
e: Combustion of sulphur-containing fuels in the smelting process emits SO2, and finally leaves sulphate on the soil. SO2 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: ____ from the atmosphere are deposited on the soil.
e: Nitrates from the atmosphere are deposited on the soil. Nitrates is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Lead particulate from automobile exhausts settles on soil along both sides of highways with heavy automobile ____.
e: Lead particulate from automobile exhausts settles on soil along both sides of highways with heavy automobile traffic. Traffic is the idea that completes this fact.

q: High levels of Pb, Zn, etc. are observed on soils near lead and ____ mines.
e: High levels of Pb, Zn, etc. are observed on soils near lead and zinc mines. Zinc is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Fertilisers and pesticides applied to crops are largely ____ by the soil.
e: Fertilisers and pesticides applied to crops are largely retained by the soil. Retained is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Fertilisers and pesticides become part of environmental cycles due to sorption by the soil and ____ into water.
e: Fertilisers and pesticides become part of environmental cycles due to sorption by the soil and leaching into water. Leaching is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Pesticides undergo degradation in soil through the processes of biodegradation, chemical degradation, or ____ reactions.
e: Pesticides undergo degradation in soil through the processes of biodegradation, chemical degradation, or photochemical reactions. Photochemical is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Insects, earthworms, plants and microorganisms play important roles in the ____ of pesticides.
e: Insects, earthworms, plants and microorganisms play important roles in the biodegradation of pesticides. Biodegradation is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Pesticide residues on crops and food products cause long-term ____.
e: Pesticide residues on crops and food products cause long-term health hazards. Health hazards is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The main sources which pollute the soil are acid rains, repeated or excess use of the same fertiliser, inadequate drainage system, and spraying plants with insecticides and ____.
e: The main sources which pollute the soil are acid rains, repeated or excess use of the same fertiliser, inadequate drainage system, and spraying plants with insecticides and herbicides. Herbicides is the idea that completes this fact.

q: ____ is the foundation of basic ecosystem function.
e: Soil is the foundation of basic ecosystem function. Soil is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Soil filters our water, provides essential nutrients to our forest and crops, and helps regulate the Earth's ____.
e: Soil filters our water, provides essential nutrients to our forest and crops, and helps regulate the Earth's temperature. Temperature is the idea that completes this fact.
